source.title: Find Maximum Area of a Triangle

teaching.hint: If one side is fixed on a vertical line, which coordinates determine its base length and its height?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: For one coordinate line, its extreme points maximize the base and a global perpendicular extreme maximizes height independently.
solution_outline.approach: Group points by x and by y, keeping each group’s opposite-coordinate minimum and maximum. Keep global extrema too. For each vertical or horizontal base line, multiply its largest span by its greatest perpendicular distance to an extreme; take the largest positive product.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: Each group stores its largest available base length, while global extrema supply the farthest possible perpendicular vertex for that line.
solution_outline.correctness: Any valid triangle has an axis-parallel side on some processed line. Its base and height are bounded by the computed extrema. The two group extremes and a farthest perpendicular point attain their product; if positive, that point is off the line and distinct from the base vertices. Thus the maximum positive product is exactly the optimal doubled area, and absence of a positive product proves no valid triangle.
solution_outline.complexity: Expected O(n) time and O(n) auxiliary space with hash grouping, or O(n log n) time with sorted groups.
solution_outline.pitfall: The longest base overall need not win: its available height depends on its coordinate line.

common_wrong_turns: The longest base overall need not win: its available height depends on its coordinate line.
source_fidelity_notes: Removed the figure; retained side orientation, distinct points, doubled area, and positive-area/-1 rules.
